public.meta.title: Quad – School management built around the child
public.meta.description: Quad runs your whole school and keeps everyone who looks after a child connected: teachers, parents and grandparents, in one circle.
public.nav.label: Sections
public.comingSoon.title: Sign-in opens when schools go live
public.comingSoon.body: Quad is getting ready for its first schools. Once your school is on Quad, you’ll sign in here with your work email. Until then, book a demo and we’ll show you around.
public.hero.eyebrow: School management, built around the child
public.hero.title: Every child has a {accent}
public.hero.lede: The teacher who notices, the coach who cheers, the bus aunty who waves, and the family waiting at home. Quad runs your whole school, from admissions to fees, and keeps every one of those people close to the child they share.
public.hero.seeDay: See a day in the circle
public.hero.fine.curricula: Cambridge, Edexcel, IB and national curricula
public.hero.fine.local: Rupees, PayHere and Poya days built in
public.hero.scene: A watercolour picture: Amaya, in her white school uniform and plaits, stands on a path between her school and her home in the tea hills, looking up. Around her in the sky drift kites, one for each person in her circle: at school Ms. Jayasinghe, Mr. Perera, Coach Herath, Nurse Dias and Sunethra on the bus; at home her mum Dilhani, her dad Ruwan and her grandmother Kamala.

public.circle.title: What is the Quad {accent}
public.circle.lede: The Circle is the small group of people at school and at home who care for one child, and the simple ways Quad keeps them in touch.

public.circle.loop.title: How the circle works
public.circle.loop.moment.title: A moment at school
public.circle.loop.moment.body: Two taps, and only Amaya’s family sees her mural.
public.circle.loop.thanks.title: Home says thanks
public.circle.loop.thanks.body: Mum taps thank you. Grandma, invited, loves it.
public.circle.loop.try.title: Try it at home
public.circle.loop.try.body: One small idea from class. They tap We tried it.
public.circle.loop.pulse.title: The teacher sees it
public.circle.loop.pulse.body: Her family pulse shows who needs good news next.
public.circle.rules.title: What keeps it kind and safe
public.circle.rules.family.title: Families choose who’s in
public.circle.rules.family.body: Parents invite up to four relatives. Relatives only see moments, and can be removed in one tap.
public.circle.rules.photos.title: Photos only with permission
public.circle.rules.photos.body: Parents choose who sees photos of their child: the class, family only, or no photos.
public.circle.rules.quiet.title: Quiet hours
public.circle.rules.quiet.body: Teachers aren’t pinged from 18:00 to 07:00 or at weekends. Urgent safety alerts still go through.
public.circle.rules.records.title: Good news, not records
public.circle.rules.records.body: Health and safeguarding notes never go into the Circle, and relatives never see fees, marks or attendance.
public.day.title: One school day in {accent}
public.day.lede: School systems are good at records and bad at relationships. Parents hear nothing until something goes wrong, and teachers get messages at 10 pm. Circle uses what a school already records to keep families close. Here is a Monday for Amaya, Year 4 Emerald.
public.day.arrive.title: Amaya’s mum sees she’s arrived
public.day.arrive.body: The gate scan and the register start a ring of Amaya’s day on her mum’s phone. Lessons, lunch and the bus home appear as they happen. Nobody had to send a message.
public.day.moment.title: Her teacher shares a moment in ten seconds
public.day.moment.body: Ms. Jayasinghe taps Amaya’s name, picks Photo, writes a line and tags the skill she noticed. Only Amaya’s family sees it, and only if the family has agreed to photos.
public.day.grandma.title: Grandma in Kandy loves it too
public.day.grandma.body: Parents can invite up to four relatives to see moments. Grandparents never see fees, results, attendance or health, and can be removed with one tap.
public.day.people.title: Dad sees who looks after Amaya
public.day.people.body: Every teacher, the coach and the nurse, with what each is working on with Amaya and when they reply. Saying thank you is one tap, and it reaches the teacher.
public.day.try.title: They try one thing at home
public.day.try.body: Each week teachers share what the class is learning and one small thing to try at home. Amaya and her mum write a postcard to Grandma, tap We tried it, and Ms. Jayasinghe sees it the next morning.
public.day.quiet.title: Teachers get their evenings back
public.day.quiet.body: A parent can still write at 19:30. Quad tells them kindly that it reaches the teacher at 07:00, and holds the teacher’s notifications until morning. Urgent safety alerts always go through.
public.day.recap.title: A week with Amaya, in one card
public.day.recap.body: The moments, the skills her teachers noticed, days in school, what the family tried at home, and one idea for the weekend.
public.day.foot: Families choose who sees photos of their child. Nothing about health or safeguarding ever goes into Circle.
public.ideas.title: Four ideas that put {accent}
public.ideas.lede: Quad is a complete school system. These are the things it does that others don’t, and the reasons schools tell us they switched.
public.ideas.story.title: Mornings start with a few plain sentences
public.ideas.story.body: Every home screen opens with what is happening and what needs you: who’s in, what’s due, what went well. The charts come after.
public.ideas.story.quote: Good morning, Prishan. 1,186 of 1,248 students are in. Three things need you today.
public.ideas.warning.title: Quad notices the child who’s drifting
public.ideas.warning.body: When a student starts to slip in attendance, homework, behaviour or marks, Quad says why and suggests who is best placed to help. One click starts a support plan.
public.ideas.warning.quote: Kavindu: History down 14 points this term, two missed submissions. Suggested: Mr. Mendis, his class teacher.
public.ideas.ask.title: Ask in plain English, see where the answer came from
public.ideas.ask.body: Quad answers from your school’s own records, names its sources, and only uses what you’re allowed to see. It never reads safeguarding or medical notes.
public.ideas.ask.quoteAnswer: Four students. From: early warning, registers.
public.ideas.brand.title: One app for every family, wearing your colours
public.ideas.brand.body: Families download one Quad app. Once they sign in it shows your school’s name, logo and colours, and says Year 4, Grade 4 or Form 1 the way you do.
public.ideas.brand.quote: Their school, not a software company.
public.leaders.title: Is every family {accent}
public.leaders.lede: One view shows which classes are sharing good news and which families haven’t heard anything positive in two weeks. It is about families, never a league table of teachers.
public.leaders.pulse.title: Family pulse for every class teacher
public.leaders.pulse.body: Families with nothing positive lately come first, with a one-tap “Share a moment about Rehan”.
public.leaders.followUp.title: A gentle follow-up list
public.leaders.followUp.body: Remind the class teacher, or send a note from the office.
public.leaders.quiet.title: Quiet hours for the whole school
public.leaders.quiet.body: Set once in Communications. Messages and moments wait until morning.
public.leaders.heat.title: Families who heard something positive
public.leaders.heat.label: Share of families who heard something positive, by year group and class
public.school.title: Everything a school runs, {accent}
public.school.lede: Turn on the modules you need. Year groups, terms and grading come from your curriculum, so Quad says Year 4, Grade 4 or Form 1 the way your school does.
public.school.modules.admissions.title: Admissions
public.school.modules.admissions.body: Enquiries, applications, interviews and offers in one pipeline
public.school.modules.students.title: Students
public.school.modules.students.body: Profiles, guardians, documents and a full history
public.school.modules.attendance.title: Attendance
public.school.modules.attendance.body: Registers in seconds, with alerts to parents at 09:00
public.school.modules.timetable.title: Timetable & cover
public.school.modules.timetable.body: A clash-free timetable, and cover for absent colleagues
public.school.modules.exams.title: Exams & reports
public.school.modules.exams.body: Exam timetables, gradebooks and report cards in your grading scale
public.school.modules.pastoral.title: Pastoral care
public.school.modules.pastoral.body: Behaviour, rewards, house points and safeguarding with strict access
public.school.modules.fees.title: Fees & finance
public.school.modules.fees.body: Billing runs, sibling discounts, PayHere and bank transfer, in rupees
public.school.modules.communication.body: Messages, news, parents’ evenings and consent forms
public.trust.title: Children’s data, {accent}
public.trust.lede: Quad is designed so each person sees only what they need, and every sensitive view is recorded.
public.trust.wall.title: Only your school
public.trust.wall.body: Each school’s data is walled off in the database itself, not just hidden in the app.
public.trust.consent.title: Families decide
public.trust.consent.body: Parents choose who sees photos of their child, and relatives only ever see moments.
public.trust.lock.title: Sensitive stays sensitive
public.trust.lock.body: Safeguarding and medical notes need special access, and every view is logged.
public.trust.local.title: Local rules
public.trust.local.body: Built for Sri Lanka’s Personal Data Protection Act, with data kept in the region.

public.demo.lede: We’ll set up a sample of your school, with your name, colours and curriculum, and walk your team through a full school day in Quad. Tea is on us.
